title: Maxinsights Raises $30M Seed Led by Peak XV for Robot Training Data
summary:
Over 5,000 contractors wearing cameras are recording real-life work in restaurants and hotels to create training datasets for robotic manipulation. Maxinsights has already captured more than 2M+ hours of this first-person footage and recently raised a $30M seed round led by Peak XV to scale its operations. The company also launched MaxLoop, which provides same-day quality scores for video clips, and MaxGlove, a device that records touch and force data that cameras cannot detect.

Maxinsights aims to accumulate 1M hours of force data by 2027 to help robots improve their grasp of objects and prevent items from slipping or cracking. The firm notes that most current robot training relies on staged movements, whereas its approach captures natural human movements in real-world environments. This tactile pressure data supplements video-only policies, which typically have to infer the physical force of a grasp based on visual shape.

selectedTweets.text:
Homes are becoming one of the richest places to collect robot training data, but its not as simple as just recording a video.

Hand force data is becoming one of the most useful signals in robot manipulation.

MaxGlove, from @Maxinsights records touch and force from people’s hands while they work, the layer of a grasp a camera can’t capture.

Pressure decides most of a grasp, whether the glass slides out or cracks. The correction when something starts to slip begins in the fingertips, usually before a camera can pick it up.

A policy trained only on video learns the shape of a grasp and has to infer the force. Glove data supplies the force directly, from people handling the objects robots will be asked to handle.

Maxinsights says it’s aiming for a million hours of force data by 2027, on top of the 2M+ hours of footage captured so far.
